claim: A property owner or aggrieved taxpayer may file a protest with the board of review on or after April 2 through April 30 of the assessment year.

Protest grounds: assessment not equitable compared with like property; assessed for more than authorized value; property not assessable, exempt or misclassified; error in assessment; fraud or misconduct (specifically stated).
Board of review decisions may be appealed to the Property Assessment Appeal Board within 20 days after the local board adjourns or May 31, whichever is later.
The taxpayer may bypass PAAB and appeal the board of review decision directly to district court.

District court appeal is filed with the clerk of district court within 20 days after the board's adjournment or May 31, whichever is later; the court hears it in equity with no presumption the assessment is correct.
Taxes on an assessment under appeal are not delayed; if reduced, taxes on the reduced portion are abated, refunded or credited.
Property is valued at actual value and, except as otherwise provided, assessed at 100 percent of actual value.

Iowa imposes a real estate transfer tax on each deed or instrument conveying realty for consideration.
Rate: eighty cents for each $500 or fractional part of $500 of actual market value in excess of $500.
No tax applies when there is no consideration, or when the instrument is a corrective instrument that so states.
The grantor (person who conveys) is liable for the tax.
A declaration of value signed by a seller, buyer or agent must be submitted to the county recorder when the deed is presented for recording.

Exemptions include deeds without consideration between spouses or parent and child, tax deeds, deeds between former spouses under a dissolution decree, deeds in lieu of foreclosure, deeds distributing assets to heirs or devisees, deeds of $500 or less, and government grantor deeds.
Consideration includes any encumbrance or lien assumed by the grantee, and the stated price is presumed to include personal property unless its value is stated on the instrument.
Iowa mortgages and deeds of trust may be foreclosed only by court action in equity, except under the alternative procedure of section 654.18.
Alternative nonjudicial voluntary foreclosure requires mutual written agreement; the mortgagor conveys all interest to the mortgagee and the mortgagee waives any deficiency.
Junior lienholders get 30 days from mailing of notice to exercise redemption rights under the voluntary procedure; mortgagor has a five-business-day cancellation right.
After a foreclosure sale the debtor may redeem within one year from the day of sale and keeps possession meanwhile; the first six months is exclusive to the debtor.
For mortgaged property under 10 acres, the mortgage may reduce the redemption period to six months (three months if not agricultural) if the mortgagee waives any deficiency.
Creditors may redeem within nine months from the day of sale if the debtor does not redeem.
For agricultural land, a creditor may not start foreclosure until it gives a notice of right to cure and waits 45 days.
